leads.area: Mathieu thin-image / actual Haar graph laws
leads.result: For algebraic edge densities, Cauchy-transform algebraicity is finite combinatorial monodromy; rationality is trivial combinatorial monodromy. Local regular branch sums constrain endpoints and crossings.
leads.fit: Pure moments force exterior transform 1/z. Compute its continuation across the actual one-outer-domain graph, including inward branches, and seek a nonzero jump cocycle.
leads.missing: Prove the actual Haar edge density is algebraic, or supply a justified period-valued extension. It is generally a moving algebraic period, not automatically an algebraic function. Endpoint poles and singular densities must be checked.
leads.obstruction_to_shortcut: The paper gives compensated branch jumps and non-composition examples. Local gluing or cancellation conditions alone do not imply a common composition factor.
leads.adoption: No identifier citation found in scanned Markdown files; compare source contents, not identifier absence, before calling the method new.
leads.next_step: For one retained exceptional real seed, derive the density and its branch/period continuation at every critical value. Test one inward-leaf configuration before claiming an all-degree obstruction.

leads.result: Moments of a meromorphic function and differential on a fixed compact Riemann surface reduce to finitely many zero-dimensional branch sums.
leads.fit: The first proposition in the accompanying TeX applies the theorem to f*omega: all positive moments force the zeroth moment zero, under its pole hypothesis. This gives a concrete obstruction to a mass-one pure Haar representation of that kind.
leads.missing: A fixed curve, a closed cycle, and poles of omega only over poles of f. Higher-dimensional Haar periods or moving curves do not meet these conditions merely by being algebraic integrals.
leads.obstruction_to_shortcut: The theorem includes the zeroth moment; the shift argument is necessary. Do not insert mass-one purity directly as its all-moments-zero hypothesis.
leads.adoption: No identifier citation found; Gavrilov occurs in other JC2 notes, so the author is not new to the repository.
leads.next_step: Check whether any natural residual Haar subclass has the fixed-curve representation. If not, explicitly retain the moving-period obstruction rather than importing the theorem.
leads.adoption_followup: Before messaging, the latest Mathieu trace and REAL_SEED_DENSITY_BOUNDS_AND_PERIOD_TRACE.md already contained a fixed-curve pole criterion and citation 1107.3029. This is overlapping work; not sent as a new result.

leads.result: For the specified oriented positive integer surgery on an L-space knot, a smooth negative-definite filling with torsion-free H1 imposes a genus deficit at least sqrt(p)+1; sharp fillings impose at least sqrt(3p+1).
leads.fit: The all-plus solid history has c=2g-1=2A-1, so p=2A-1 and p=2A+1 fail the nonsharp necessary bound. This goes beyond the L-space genus endpoint test if an actual filling is available.
leads.missing: Identify the actual oriented closed surgery and a filling with the stated homology. The familiar surgery trace has the wrong sign in general. Solidity is three-dimensional, not this hypothesis.
leads.adoption: No identifier or changemaker citation found in the Markdown scan. Existing Ni-Wu and graph-gluing inputs already adopted.
leads.next_step: Audit the actual complementary survivor plumbing and its orientation. Only after that check deficit inequalities or characteristic covectors; do not run a coefficient search first.
leads.related_result: McCoy Theorem 3.5 provides rational-surgery changemaker lattices under sharp-filling assumptions. Theorem 1.1 determines Alexander polynomials at sufficiently large common surgery slopes; this is not automatic knot recognition.

leads.result: Knotification and generalized correction terms constrain configurations of singularities on projective curves. The explicit Theorem 6.4 allows cusps and positive T(2,2n) singularities.
leads.fit: Global algebraic realization can impose constraints not visible to local linking or an individual splice. Multibranch singularities need not force a return to cuspidal-only tests.
leads.missing: Construct the actual projective curve with its degree, geometric genus, all singular links, and the required complement. A formal peripheral packet or an arbitrary iterated knot at infinity is insufficient.
leads.next_step: Translate one surviving ruled-boundary configuration into a genuine curve, or document precisely why that translation is unavailable.
leads.related_result: Borodzik-Livingston gives rational cuspidal plane-curve semigroup restrictions. Borodzik-Moe gives Hirzebruch-surface semigroup and spectral restrictions; use the correct ambient surface and hypotheses.

leads.result: For a fixed finite-presentation coefficient scheme over the specified Henselian valuation ring, sufficiently precise approximate points can be corrected to exact ones with prescribed lower precision.
leads.fit: The third proposition gives finite-precision detection of nonliftability at fixed degree without assuming compatible approximations. Over O_Cp it also gives a fixed-ring valuation threshold.
leads.missing: The theorem is not effective here, not uniform in degree or arbitrary changes of base ring, and does not solve global plane-Keller divisor recovery.
leads.adoption: No Greenberg citation found. Artin approximation is discussed in the separate Dixmier formal-lifting notes. HC4 coefficient-closure already proves more explicit bounds for the retained nonplane/collision controls.
leads.next_step: Use only for coefficient-lifting cases not already covered by the product-ideal obstruction; avoid duplicating the stronger retained result.

leads.version: PDF v2, 5 August 2026: Algebraic Cauchy transforms of real algebraic ovals. Abstract-page title/summary differs; use the checked PDF statement.
leads.result: A separating lifted oval gives an incomplete-trace formula. Under two-transitive monodromy and non-descending meromorphic density, algebraicity of the stated closed-lift transform is equivalent to separation.
leads.fit: Suggests a homology and representation obstruction after constructing the relevant lifted cycle and meromorphic density. Also warns that positive genus alone does not force transcendence.
leads.missing: Its exterior domain transform is for uniform planar area. General theorem still requires a smooth Jordan curve with a closed diffeomorphic lift and meromorphic density. Haar graph laws do not automatically fit.
leads.next_step: Treat as a comparison model, below the general graph-monodromy approach, until a valid Haar lift is supplied.

leads.result: Under moment-determinacy conditions, high powers or polynomial ideals can be dense in the appropriate positive L2 space.
leads.fit: Possible analytic alternative for excluding eventual orthogonality in real-seed subclasses.
leads.missing: A polynomial Gaussian pushforward need not be moment-determinate. Non-discreteness alone does not justify determinacy. Complex phases also require their actual positive-pairing reduction.
leads.adoption: No identifier citation found; retained algebraic Gaussian pairing already gives the needed thin-image bad-marker theorem.
leads.next_step: Do not divert the Gaussian work merely to reproduce a result already proved by the stronger finite-module method.
